what: The player's language model becomes a named setting (`--model`) on every run and score, recorded in run.json and the score file. A named model's score lands in <set>.<slug>.score.json beside the committed scores. Each goal records its target's validity and its words. A compare command writes a loss report of two models' scores. GLM-5.3-flash and Haiku 5.5 are scored on the built code over the four goal sets and the report is committed, with the default left at Haiku.

criteria.given: two sets of score files written by this code for a baseline and a candidate model in a temp directory, with each goal's run.json under the run paths they name. Set one has a goal the baseline held and the candidate did not, its candidate run stuck with a recorded target and steps. Set two has a goal the candidate held and the baseline did not, and a goal whose candidate target was refused with stopped kind parse. Every goal has words of each kind across the two models.
criteria.when: tests/compare.test.ts (new) runs `bun run compare --baseline <b> --candidate <c> --goals <set one> --goals <set two>`
criteria.then: it exits 0 and writes <c-slug>.vs.<b-slug>.compare.json and .compare.md beside the first goal file. Per set, they show each model's reached held of of, targets valid of asked, words written and refused, and costUsd with unreportedCosts, equal to the score files' values. Losses list exactly the goals the baseline held and the candidate did not, each with both models' outcome and the target or stopped read from its own run.json. Gains list exactly the reverse. The words section lists every goal with both models' words. No key or line in either file states held, holds, did-not-hold or a verdict for a set or the whole. The markdown carries the same numbers and goal ids as the JSON.

outOfScope.summary: Each model is scored once per set, so a goal listed as lost or gained can be run-to-run noise rather than the model (calibration went from 8 of 9 to 9 of 9 between two committed Haiku scores); the report shows the recorded target and outcome of each so rudy can read which, and a re-run is his call.

frequency.records: goals of corpus/goals/calibration.baseline.score.json and calibration.moved.score.json, two Haiku scores of calibration on the same rule (harness-package)

outOfScope.summary: Naming the default model on the command line writes a separate <set>.<slug>.score.json rather than the registered <set>.score.json, so the same model can have two score files for one set.

frequency.reason: No reader confuses the two: C9 and the committed record read <set>.score.json by name, and compare reads only the named-model files and checks each one's model field.

outOfScope.summary: Score files written before this carry no model, targets or words field, and the committed runs are not rewritten; compare reads only files written by this code.
complete() sends the same request to both models, json_object with no max_tokens and no structured-output schema, so GLM is measured on today's request rather than one tuned for it.

frequency.reason: This is the like-for-like comparison issue #3 asks for, not a usage path. GLM answered that exact request shape with parseable JSON (docs/work/model-setting/shape/glm-probe.txt).

stakes: The player's model is one setting, `--model`, on every run and score; with none named the target and words are asked of anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5, as today.
A model id that is not <provider>/<model> is refused at the command line with exit 2, before any bench boots or any call is made.
Every run.json's parameters.wordsModel and every new score file's model name the model the runs were made with.
A score made under a named model writes only <set>.<slug>.score.json and never writes, reads or replaces <set>.score.json, so C9's calibration record and every committed score stay byte-identical.
Each goal's score entry says whether its target answer was schema-valid, schema-invalid or never answered, and whether its words were written (with the line) or refused; each score file sums them.

compare writes a loss report and no verdict. Per set, it puts both models' reached count, schema-valid targets of asked, words written and refused, and cost side by side. Then, in order, it lists every goal the baseline held and the candidate did not (with both models' outcome and recorded target or refusal), every goal the reverse, and every goal's words from both models, all rendered by code from the score and run files.
compare refuses two score files that name another model, were made at other thresholds than the registered ones, or score other goals, so the report only ever sets like-for-like runs side by side.

GLM-5.3-flash and Haiku 5.5 are each scored once per set on the same built code over calibration, blind-1, blind-2-spent and blind-2, and the scores, their runs and the comparison are committed together.
A comparison run that a provider failed (target unanswered) halts the job for a ruling; it is never counted for or against a model, and never silently re-run.
The default model is not changed; Jev's model stays a constant; the harness still reads the world only over the bench's routes.
